title: Maximal tame extension and its Galois p-property
statement: All fields below are fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values. For such a field $A$, write $A^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ for its valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde A=A^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_A=|A^\times|$. For a finite extension $B/A$ set $e(B/A)=[\Gamma_B:\Gamma_A]$, $f(B/A)=[\widetilde B:\widetilde A]$ and $d(B/A)=[B:A]/(e(B/A)f(B/A))$. Call it immediate if its value group and residue field equal those of $A$, unramified if $e=d=1$ and the residue extension is separable, and tame if $d=1$, its residue extension is separable and its ramification index is prime to the residue characteristic (with no index restriction in residue characteristic zero). A field extension is separable if every algebraic element has a minimal polynomial with distinct roots. Let $A$ be complete with $p=\operatorname{char}(\widetilde A)>0$, and fix an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $A$ with the extending absolute value. Let $T\subseteq\Omega$ be the union of all intermediate fields $A\subseteq A_0\subseteq\Omega$ such that $A_0/A$ is finite tame. Then $T$ is a field, these finite tame subextensions form a nonempty directed family, and every finite subextension of $T/A$ is tame. Every finite Galois field extension $N/T$ has degree a power of $p$. Here Galois means normal and separable, normal means that every irreducible polynomial over the base with a root in the extension splits there, and finite degree means vector-space dimension.
